title: My AI screener flagged SELL on NFLX, ADBE, AMZN, and INTU at the same time this morning
author: Medicine_Blogscanner
selftext:
Not posting this as a trade recommendation - just thought the simultaneous signal cluster across large-cap tech was worth sharing.

All four showing RSI in the 36-39 range, Risk/Reward at 1.50, expected move between 2.5-5%. The screener runs on my phone locally - no cloud, signals generated on-device.

Anyone else seeing weakness in large-cap tech right now? Curious if others are tracking the same setup.

replies.author: AdmirableJudgment784
replies.body: Where does your bot access recent price data? My bot could only get the market close data.

replies.author: Medicine_Blogscanner
replies.body:
Good question. The app supports multiple market data providers - you can connect your own API key from supported sources, or use the built-in provider that comes with the subscription. The data quality and freshness depends on which provider is configured.
For on-demand scans outside market hours (like the weekend scan in this post), it's using the most recent available price data - so end-of-day on Friday in this case, same as what your bot would have. The signals aren't based on live tick data during a weekend scan, they're based on the last known close plus the indicators derived from it.
Real-time intraday data is available during market hours depending on your data provider setup. So the short answer: it's not magic - same data universe you're working with, just a different model layer on top of it.

replies.author: Medicine_Blogscanner
replies.body:
Happy to share the background. The TradeMAV team has been building this ecosystem for a while - it started as a USB hardware device (a portable AI screener you plug into your laptop) that ran all inference locally with no subscription. We Kickstarter-funded it with 338 backers across the US, India, UK, Australia, and Canada, which validated the on-device approach before we built anything else.

From there we expanded into ForexMAV (same engine, forex-focused), later OptionMAV for options and most recently launched the Android app so the signal engine runs directly on your phone without needing the USB hardware at all.

The core architecture in the app - ONNX model inference on the device, AES-256 encrypted model storage, no trading data leaving your phone during a scan. The USB owners get personally trained models synced to the app; app-only subscribers get our hosted models through the same encrypted pipeline.

If you want to dig into it — trademav.com has the full product overview, and the Android app has a 7-day free demo: play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.trademav.app

comments.author: Left-Necessary8405
comments.body:
I tried making a scanner last week and realised there’s so much detail in WHAT you use for a signal. 

It’s like… either you have to use very broad based indicators, or you need to get far more granular with it, which means really choosing all those very carefully. That is the part which makes it very hard. 

I will say I can’t wait to make one because most screeners don’t LOOK very good and aren’t anywhere near as organized like they should be. 

I’m thinking one method is to find gold scanners that already exist, also perhaps quality free or paid signals. Then have the AI create a system where one can take all of those signals and test how well they could create a signal of confluence, and then put the data on the chart. In the same way as you can find crypto platforms which let you see where some wallet traded. 

 Just imagine if you have multiple scanners and “trading signals” cluster near the same location. I mean it depends on how good the scanner is and how good the signals are but there ARE good signal sources out there, but be able to see the confluence should allow you to get a significantly strong signal! Like imagine if one signal source posted the opposite signal to another that you also like. This would let you easily see that discrepancy and therefore decide to leave that one maybe. 

And of course one can still use your own technical analysis, but I don’t see why one can’t take a broadly +50% technical accurate win rate and increase that to at least 70-80 or even 90% depending on how good your signal sources are, and how much you’re filtering for the strongest setups

replies.author: Medicine_Blogscanner
replies.body: The granularity problem is real. Most scanners fail because they pick indicators without understanding what regime they work in. What you're describing - confluence scoring across multiple signal sources - is a solid approach. The risk is "garbage-in": if the inputs aren't independently validated, confluence just amplifies the same bias.

comments.author: Ok-Lobster-919
comments.body:
For fun I had my AI agent analyze your signals. It has some criticisms you should look into. 

    The TradeMAV signals are right about ONE thing: all four stocks are in downtrends. The model correctly identifies bearish Ichimoku, bearish MACD (except INTU), bearish ADX/DMI, below all major MAs.
    
    But here's what the signals miss:
    
    1. All four are at or near multi-month oversold extremes (Z-scores -0.77 to -1.21)
    2. All four have bullish stochastic crossovers firing
    3. Mean reversion half-lives are 2.4-11.1 days — bounces happen
    4. The quant models themselves show contradictory bullish signals (especially INTU and AMZN)
    5. AMZN has institutional accumulation despite the SELL signal
    6. INTU's MACD just crossed bullish — classic momentum reversal
    7. NFLX is at its 52-week low — major support test
    
    The signals are trend-following trades entering at potential mean reversion points. That's fighting the math.
    
    My Honest Assessment
    
    If I had to deploy capital on this cluster, I'd take ONE position:
    • NFLX (highest conviction: 55%) — strongest trend, no MACD bullish cross yet, at 52W low with clear support test
    
    I'd pass on:
    • INTU — model contradicts itself, MACD bullish crossover, only -6% to major support
    • AMZN — institutional accumulation, only -16% from 52W high, +2.73% YTD
    • ADBE — best RR but support too close to current price; -6% to pivot S1 with a 9.6% stop is uncomfortable
    
    Issues:
    
    The signal timestamps are 12:08:31, 12:08:35, 12:08:47, 12:08:54 — within 23 seconds of each other. This is a systematic model firing on correlated signals, not independent analysis. The model sees similar setups and applies the same template — which is why the RR is exactly 1.50 across all four.
    
    All four stocks were up +2.5% to +5% Friday. The signals are "sell the bounce" trades. In an established downtrend this works — but after 15-25% monthly drops with bullish stochastic crossovers firing, you're fading a possible trend reversal, not a normal retracement.
    
    The TradeMAV stops are 12-15% below current price, but actual technical support (pivot S1, 52W low) is only 4-6% away. The stops are positioned below major support — meaning the model is betting on support breaks. When that many correlated names all have support within 4-6%, either they all break (correlated crash) or they all hold (correlated bounce).
    
    All four are mega-cap tech/consumer names. If next week brings:
    • Fed pivot speculation → All four rally
    • Iran escalation → Mixed (could lift NFLX/AMZN, hurt ADBE/INTU differently)
    • Tech earnings beats → All four squeeze
    • Macro risk-off → All four drop together
    
    The correlation means diversification benefits are minimal — these are essentially four expressions of the same bet.

replies.author: Medicine_Blogscanner
replies.body:
Fair points, and mostly accurate. A few clarifications on how it's actually wired:

The near-identical timestamps are expected - TradeMAV runs the whole watchlist in a single batch pass, so correlated names fire within seconds. The uniform RR follows from the same risk formula applied per signal: similar volatility + confidence = similar RR. That's by construction, not a bug.

The threshold editor is real and configurable - it controls signal qualification (RSI, momentum, ADX sensitivity), not just a cosmetic label.

Where your AI agent is right: correlation risk is real when mega-caps cluster, "retracement vs. reversal" is the call no screener can make for you, and position sizing is still on the trader.

One correction worth noting: stop/target values on the signal card are model-calculated at scan time. If you want a custom ongoing risk/exit plan, that's what Exit Monitoring controls are for - not something overridden at the individual signal card level.

7-day demo: [play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.trademav.app](http://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.trademav.app)

Great question. TradeMAV works with any stocks you add to your watchlist, so yes, Indian market stocks are supported - NSE/BSE tickers work.

That said, a quick heads up for a beginner: the app surfaces AI-generated signals with entry, stop, and target levels, but it's designed as a decision-support tool, not an autopilot. You still decide whether to act on a signal. If you're new to trading, it can actually be a good learning tool - the signals come with RSI, confidence scores, and risk/reward context that help you understand why a setup is flagged.

replies.author: Medicine_Blogscanner
replies.body:
Fair push. The signals aren't just "RSI in 30s and LED flashing" - here's what's actually under the hood:
The model evaluates RSI, MACD, ADX, Ichimoku, stochastic crossovers, and momentum together - not any single indicator in isolation. A SELL signal fires when the confluence of those factors crosses the model's threshold for a bearish setup. All four names in this cluster hit that threshold within the same scan window, which is what made it worth posting.

The "why" on each signal card shows confidence score, expected move range, and risk/reward — so you're not flying blind. Whether you act on it is still your call.
